title: M/s Tirupati Cylinders Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Krishna Murari and Vijay Lakshmi, JJ. (30.4.2014); Dilip B. Bhosale, C.J. and Yashwant Varma, J. (27.2.2017)
disposition: Writ disposed as infructuous; 4.20 demand undecided
headnote: A consumer's writ to quash a demand for additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was disposed of as infructuous on counsel's statement that the petition had become infructuous with time. The High Court did not decide the demand. An earlier Division Bench had, without prejudice and following a similar pending writ, restrained the licensee from demanding additional security until further orders.
facts: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. issued a 2 April 2014 demand notice requiring M/s Tirupati Cylinders Ltd. of Muzaffarnagar to furnish additional security under paragraph 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer sought quashing of that notice, pointing to an interim order of 7 October 2009 in a similar writ by M/s Supreme Ceramics Limited. A Division Bench connected the petitions and, without prejudice, restrained the licensee from demanding additional security until further orders. In 2017 counsel stated that the writ had become infructuous with time.

holding_units.holding: A writ seeking to quash a licensee's demand for additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was disposed of as infructuous on the petitioner's statement that the petition had become infructuous with the passage of time; the demand was not decided on merits. Earlier, a Division Bench had connected the matter with a similar pending writ and, without prejudice to the parties' rights, restrained the licensee from demanding additional security until further orders.

not_decided.point: Whether additional security could be demanded under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
not_decided.note: Petition disposed of as infructuous without examining the demand notice dated 02.04.2014
